title: interactional-features-ja: quantifying interactional features of Japanese everyday conversation
description:
Reproducible pipeline for measuring 19 interactional features (speech timing, fillers, sequence organisation, response types) from Japanese everyday conversation, together with the validation analyses reported in the accompanying manuscript.

All five trait dimensions are analysed at equal granularity. The reported model regresses the language-model trait scores on the 19 features plus speaker sex and age, so every association is estimated with those attributes held constant. The evaluation comprises Ridge regression under a subject-wise GroupKFold split on speaker identity, permutation tests with Holm correction across dimensions, coefficient-level permutation tests combined with bootstrap stability, sensitivity analyses over preprocessing, regularisation strength and cross-validation choices, an estimate of the effect size the design can detect, and baseline conditions that test whether the language-model scores depend on the transcript content. Correlation, coefficient of determination and RMSE are reported together, since ridge shrinkage makes a correlation alone a weak summary of fit.

The CEJC corpus is not redistributed here; it is available to researchers from the National Institute for Japanese Language and Linguistics under its own terms of use. The identity of the text shown to the models is pinned by a SHA-256 digest recorded in the repository. See docs/data-availability.md.
